knowledge_point.title: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+3y &=8\\ 3x+9y &=24.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 3 & 8 \\ 3 & 9 & 24 \end{bmatrix}
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 3 & 8 \\ 3 & 9 & 24 \end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 3 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+3y &=8\\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+3y=8.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=8-3y,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=8-3y\\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 8-3y \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+4y &=4\\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=4-4y\\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 4-4y \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}

knowledge_point.title: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3y &=-8\\ -12x+36y &=112.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & -8 \\ -12 & 36 & 112 \end{bmatrix}
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & -8 \\ -12 & 36 & 112 \end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+12{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 16 \end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3y &=-8\\ 0x+0y &=16.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=16$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=16,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.
